MARTA KOWAL-BRANDT
DevOps / Cloud Infrastructure Engineer | QA Automation Engineer
Wroclaw, Poland | marta.kowalbrandt@example.com | +48 555 303 303 | gitlab.com/mkb-example

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
QA automation engineer with 7 years of experience, including hands-on work building CI/CD pipelines, ephemeral test environments and build tooling. Experienced with GitLab CI, Docker, Helm and namespace-level Kubernetes deployments, and with improving pipeline speed, reliability and observability. Personal infrastructure projects include a k3s cluster managed with GitOps and Terraform-provisioned Hetzner VPS infrastructure. Currently preparing for the Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) exam.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Infrastructure and delivery: GitLab CI, Jenkins, Docker, Docker Compose, Helm, Kubernetes (namespace-level access), k3s, Argo CD, Terraform (personal project)
Monitoring and security: Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, Traefik, cert-manager, TLS certificate management
Programming and data: Python, Bash, Java (test code), SQL, PostgreSQL
Testing: pytest, Playwright, Selenium, Postman
Systems: Linux, Git, Ansible (basic)
Cloud learning: AWS free tier (EC2 and S3 basics); no professional cloud-platform experience

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE
QA Automation Engineer (Test Infrastructure) | Odrava Health Software, Wroclaw | 2021–Present
- Own GitLab CI pipelines for three product teams (~25 developers), covering build, unit, integration and end-to-end test stages, plus artifact publishing.
- Reduced average pipeline time from 38 to 14 minutes by profiling workflows, parallelising test jobs, caching dependencies and separating end-to-end tests into their own stage; monthly CI runner costs decreased by about 30%.
- Built merge-request ephemeral environments with Docker Compose and later Helm on the shared Kubernetes cluster. Each environment includes the application, PostgreSQL and seeded data; it is automatically removed after merge or 48 hours of inactivity.
- Maintain a pytest and Playwright end-to-end suite of approximately 900 tests; reduced the flaky-test rate from 7% to below 1%.
- Built a Python and PostgreSQL pipeline-results collection workflow and Grafana dashboards to identify flaky tests by team.
- Wrote Bash and Python tooling to seed PostgreSQL test data.
- Authored an internal guide to CI pipelines used in onboarding; mentored two QA interns in 2023.

QA Engineer | Brightmill Software House, Wroclaw | 2019–2021
- Tested web and mobile applications through manual and automated testing for client projects.
- Introduced a Java and Selenium automated regression suite for the largest client project.
- Configured Jenkins jobs to run nightly regression tests.

Customer Support Specialist (2nd line) | Brightmill Software House | 2018–2019
- Investigated customer issues using logs and databases, and reproduced bugs for developers.

SELECTED INFRASTRUCTURE PROJECTS
Homelab k3s Cluster with GitOps | Personal | 2024–2025
- Built a three-node Raspberry Pi 5 k3s cluster and deployed applications from a Git repository using Argo CD.
- Set up Prometheus, Grafana and Loki for monitoring, Traefik ingress, and cert-manager for TLS.
- Provisioned infrastructure for a small Hetzner VPS using Terraform; used Ansible at a basic level.

Merge-Request Ephemeral Environments | Odrava Health | 2023–2024
- Implemented short-lived environments for each merge request, deployed through GitLab CI and Helm to the shared Kubernetes cluster.
- Enabled QA and product teams to review features before merge and run end-to-end tests against the environment.
- Automated environment cleanup after merge or 48 hours of inactivity.

CI Pipeline Speed-up | Odrava Health | 2022
- Profiled pipelines for three teams, parallelised test jobs, introduced dependency caching and separated end-to-end tests into a dedicated stage.
- Reduced average pipeline time from 38 to 14 minutes and monthly CI runner costs by about 30%.

EDUCATION
BEng, Computer Engineering | Silesian Lowlands University of Technology | 2018

CERTIFICATIONS AND PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT
ISTQB Foundation Level | 2019
Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) preparation | Exam scheduled for January 2027

LANGUAGES
Polish (native), English (C1), German (A2)

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, well-structured CV with clear section headings, quantified achievements, relevant technical projects, and good professional transparency about the candidate's level of Kubernetes, Terraform, and cloud experience. The strongest evidence is the CI/CD ownership, 38-to-14-minute pipeline improvement, 30% runner-cost reduction, ephemeral environments, 900-test automation suite, and flaky-test reduction. The main content limitation is that the CV presents substantial DevOps-adjacent experience but gives limited direct evidence of systems architecture, infrastructure design decisions, networking beyond TLS, security practices, or stakeholder leadership at the level expected for this contractor role. The wording is otherwise credible and professional, and no unsupported qualifications or experiences were detected when cross-referenced with the Original Candidate Information.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is highly parseable: it uses conventional headings, plain text formatting, standard chronology, and keyword-rich descriptions. It includes relevant terms such as GitLab CI, Docker, Helm, Kubernetes, k3s, Argo CD, Terraform, Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, Traefik, cert-manager, TLS, Linux, Python, Bash, and PostgreSQL. Its likely ATS and AI-screening performance is good for junior-to-mid DevOps, platform, CI/CD, or test-infrastructure roles, but only moderate for this particular contractor vacancy because the document does not contain supported evidence for Terragrunt, strong Terraform, mTLS, cloud environment operation in AWS or another major cloud, or system design. The explicit statements about personal Terraform use and lack of professional cloud-platform experience improve credibility and prevent misleading keyword matching.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV aligns well with hands-on infrastructure engineering through GitLab CI ownership, Docker and Helm-based ephemeral environments, namespace-level Kubernetes work, observability tooling, and the personal k3s/GitOps/Terraform project. It also demonstrates analytical thinking, reliability improvement, clear technical documentation, mentoring, and some stakeholder enablement through QA and product-team use of merge-request environments. However, the candidate's material indicates gaps against strong Terraform and Terragrunt, production cloud design and operation, mTLS, IoT or remote-device integration, and backend/full-stack engineering. AWS is present only as free-tier learning, and the material does not establish professional AWS experience. The CV is therefore a credible but developmental match rather than a strong match for a contractor expected to shape production fleet-connectivity architecture from the start.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL / HIGH-VALUE IMPROVEMENTS:
1. In the headline, consider changing "DevOps / Cloud Infrastructure Engineer | QA Automation Engineer" to "DevOps / Infrastructure Engineer | QA Automation Engineer" or "DevOps / Platform Engineering Candidate | QA Automation Engineer". This better reflects that the documented professional experience is CI/CD and test infrastructure, while cloud infrastructure is currently represented by personal projects and learning rather than professional cloud-platform operation.

2. In the Professional Summary, add the strongest supported leadership and stakeholder evidence. For example, revise the final part to: "Owns CI/CD and test-environment improvements for three product teams, documents internal platform usage for onboarding, and enables QA and product teams to review and test changes in isolated environments." This uses the candidate's existing evidence without implying formal infrastructure-team leadership.

3. In the Odrava Health Software experience section, revise the ephemeral-environment bullet to explicitly include the stakeholder outcome: "Built merge-request ephemeral environments with Docker Compose and later Helm on the shared Kubernetes cluster, enabling QA and product teams to review features and run end-to-end tests before merge; automated cleanup after merge or 48 hours of inactivity." This more directly addresses the advert's emphasis on supporting teams and bringing stakeholders along.

4. In the Selected Infrastructure Projects section, add the omitted "Flaky Test Dashboard" project after "CI Pipeline Speed-up": "Flaky Test Dashboard | Odrava Health | 2023 — Collected GitLab CI test results through the GitLab API into PostgreSQL and built Grafana dashboards showing flaky tests by team; helped teams reduce the flaky-test rate from 7% to below 1%. Technologies: Python, PostgreSQL, Grafana, GitLab API." This strengthens evidence for analytical thinking, observability, reliability, and backend/data tooling.

5. In the Homelab k3s Cluster project, make the scope and security evidence more explicit without overstating it. Change the relevant bullets to: "Configured Traefik ingress and cert-manager for TLS certificate management" and "Provisioned a small Hetzner VPS with Terraform and used Ansible at a basic level." Retain the personal-project label so the document remains clear that this is not professional cloud-platform experience.

MINOR ATS / CLARITY IMPROVEMENTS:
6. In Technical Skills, change "Terraform (personal project)" to "Infrastructure as Code: Terraform (personal Hetzner project)". This adds the supported infrastructure-as-code terminology while preserving the important scope limitation.

7. In Technical Skills, change "TLS certificate management" to "SSL/TLS certificate management with cert-manager" only if the candidate is comfortable using the SSL/TLS wording for the documented cert-manager work. Do not add "mTLS," Terragrunt, AWS production, or cloud architecture because those capabilities are not supported by the Original Candidate Information.

8. In the Professional Experience section under Odrava Health, change "Own GitLab CI pipelines" to "Own and improve GitLab CI/CD pipelines". This better matches the job advert's terminology while remaining supported by the documented build, test, artifact, caching, parallelisation, and deployment work.

Claims the sources (the candidate's own material; for the employer, the job ad and company research) do not support:
- DevOps / Cloud Infrastructure Engineer

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, professional and unusually evidence-based CV for a QA-to-DevOps transition. It uses quantified outcomes effectively: pipeline time reduced from 38 to 14 minutes, runner costs reduced by about 30%, and flaky tests reduced from 7% to below 1%. The structure is clear, the career progression is understandable, and the distinction between professional, personal and learning experience is appropriately transparent. The main content limitation is that the CV presents a broad DevOps profile while the candidate's strongest evidence is CI/CD, test infrastructure and Kubernetes application-level work rather than full cloud-platform ownership. Some project entries duplicate achievements already described under Professional Experience, using valuable space without adding much new evidence.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is highly parseable: it uses conventional headings, plain text job titles, reverse-chronological employment history, standard technology names and no tables, columns, graphics or unusual symbols. It contains useful target keywords including infrastructure, CI/CD, Terraform, Kubernetes, Helm, Linux, TLS, monitoring, observability, AWS, Docker, GitOps and system-related delivery concepts. AI screening probability is moderate to good for junior or mid-level DevOps/platform roles, but lower for this particular vacancy because the document does not demonstrate Terragrunt, mTLS, professional AWS or other major-cloud operation, system design, or broader networking/security ownership. The explicit statement that there is no professional cloud-platform experience is truthful and useful, but it also makes the cloud-experience gap immediately visible.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV aligns well with the role's engineering-led and ownership-oriented aspects. It demonstrates ownership of CI/CD for three teams, stakeholder enablement for QA and product teams, analytical improvement work, documentation, mentoring, observability and reliable short-lived environments. The personal k3s/GitOps project adds credible infrastructure initiative and shows Terraform, Linux, monitoring, ingress and certificate-management exposure. However, the role is centered on designing and operating cloud infrastructure for production fleet connectivity. The candidate's material shows no Terragrunt, no mTLS, no IoT, automotive or remote-device integration, no professional AWS/cloud-platform operation, no production on-call ownership, and no evidence of leading architecture proposals or negotiating interfaces with external engineering stakeholders. These are candidate-profile gaps rather than defects that can be solved by wording. Java is present primarily as test code, not as backend/JVM development.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL ISSUES / HIGH-VALUE CHANGES
1. In the Professional Summary, make the scope of infrastructure ownership more precise while preserving the strong DevOps positioning. Replace the opening sentence with: "QA automation engineer with 7 years of experience, including hands-on CI/CD engineering, ephemeral test-environment design and build tooling, and additional personal Kubernetes, GitOps and Terraform infrastructure work." This avoids implying production cloud-platform ownership that the candidate has not documented.

2. In the Professional Summary, explicitly surface the strongest stakeholder and technical-leadership evidence. Add after the sentence about isolated environments: "Owns CI/CD and test-environment improvements for three product teams, documents platform usage for onboarding, and mentors junior QA engineers." The current summary mentions ownership and documentation but omits the mentoring evidence and does not make the leadership aspect as prominent as the job requires.

3. In the Technical Skills section, rename "Infrastructure and delivery" to "Infrastructure engineering and delivery" and add the supported terms "ephemeral environments," "GitOps" and "observability" to that line. For example: "Infrastructure engineering and delivery: GitLab CI, Jenkins, Docker, Docker Compose, Helm, Kubernetes (namespace-level access), k3s, Argo CD, ephemeral environments, GitOps, observability." These terms are supported by the experience and projects and improve alignment with the vacancy.

4. In the Technical Skills section, change "Monitoring and security" to "Monitoring, networking and security" only if the following wording is used exactly: "Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, Traefik ingress, cert-manager, TLS certificate management." Do not add mTLS, network design or security technologies that are not supported by the candidate information. This presents the existing networking-adjacent evidence more accurately without overstating it.

5. In the Odrava Health Software experience, revise the ephemeral-environment bullet to make the systems involved and operational outcome more directly relevant to the job. Change it to: "Designed and operated merge-request ephemeral environments using Docker Compose and later Helm on a shared Kubernetes cluster; each environment included the application, PostgreSQL and seeded data, with automated cleanup after merge or 48 hours of inactivity." "Designed and operated" is supported by the documented implementation and better reflects infrastructure engineering than "Built" alone.

6. In the Odrava Health Software experience, add the stakeholder outcome to the same ephemeral-environment bullet or the following bullet: "Enabled QA and product teams to review changes and run end-to-end tests in isolated environments before merge." This evidence is currently present in the summary and project section but should appear directly under the relevant employment entry for ATS and recruiter review.

7. In the Odrava Health Software experience, strengthen the technical-leadership and communication evidence by changing the onboarding bullet to: "Authored the internal guide to CI pipeline usage used in onboarding and mentored two QA interns in 2023." This is more concrete and uses the candidate's documented wording.

8. Reduce duplication between Professional Experience and Selected Infrastructure Projects. Keep the detailed implementation bullets under Odrava Health, but shorten the duplicate project entries to two or three lines each, or remove the duplicate "Merge-Request Ephemeral Environments" and "CI Pipeline Speed-up" entries. Preserve the unique personal k3s project and flaky-test dashboard because they add distinct infrastructure and observability evidence. This will make the CV more concise without losing quantified achievements.

MINOR, TARGETED ENHANCEMENTS
9. In the Homelab k3s Cluster project, change "configured Traefik ingress and cert-manager for TLS certificate management" to "configured Traefik ingress and cert-manager for TLS certificate management in a personal k3s environment." This keeps the TLS evidence clearly scoped and avoids any implication that it was production fleet or enterprise cloud infrastructure.

10. In the Terraform skills line, change "Terraform (personal Hetzner project)" to "Terraform (personal Hetzner VPS infrastructure project)" and retain the separate AWS line. This makes the infrastructure scope more concrete and improves keyword relevance without suggesting professional Terraform or cloud-platform experience.

11. In the certification section, retain "Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) preparation | Exam scheduled for January 2027" exactly as a preparation item, not as a certification. Do not label it "CKA" under Certifications or imply that it has been passed.
